findings.title: Dollar-quoted SQL value is misread as a line comment and masks following domain DELETE
findings.contract: Other domain writes, mixed statements and SQL values/comments cannot hide actual writes; unresolved grammar cannot receive quota exemption.
findings.explanation: normalizeSql has single/double quote modes but no dollar quote mode. -- inside $$...$$ or $value$...$value$ discards the rest of the decoded literal as a comment. Remaining INSERT target is exempted, or a remaining SELECT has no write finding. These are literal statements, not constructed SQL. No SQL was executed.

findings.title: Executable host calls pass when the callee syntax is optional, parenthesized, escaped, generic or property based
findings.contract: Executable fetch/sendMessage/HTTP effects forbidden, including executable template interpolations.
findings.explanation: The parser recognizes CallExpression, but the scanner flattens its syntax and matches name followed immediately by an opening parenthesis. It misses optional calls, parentheses, escaped identifiers, TypeScript type arguments and HTTP methods. Separately appended template AST text is still subjected to this incomplete regex. parse-proof.json independently shows valid AST calls and zero diagnostics for each failing fixture.

findings.title: Quota target alone admits unresolved UPDATE grammar
findings.contract: Unknown grammar cannot receive quota exemption.
findings.explanation: The write-intent fallback calls the same target-only allowBoundary check. An incomplete UPDATE with no SET, and UPDATE followed by an opaque template expression, receive PASS because their first target is api_rate_limit_buckets. The incomplete case is a qualification fail-closed defect, not a claim that invalid SQL executed a domain effect.

findings.title: Inert host text and read-only quoted SQL identifiers are mistaken for executable effects
findings.contract: Preserve actual benign strings/templates and read-only SQL while detecting effects.
findings.explanation: An ordinary string or non-interpolated template containing fetch(...) or sendMessage(...) has no executable call nodes but is rejected. In SELECT, double-quoted identifiers containing DELETE FROM or UPDATE ... SET are scanned as statements and rejected. They are identifier text, not writes.
